## Bring us a client. Keep 15% of the fee.

Agencies, freelancers, media buyers, community owners — if you can put a real project in front of us, you earn on every payment we clear. No cost, no exclusivity, and nothing you have to sell yourself.

### You introduce

One email with the client's need, or just forward theirs. You don't write the proposal — we do that.

### We quote & build

We scope it, price it and deliver it. Stay in the loop or stay out of it entirely — your call.

### Client pays

Payment clears in USDT or on escrow. Every payment is visible to you, on-chain.

### You get paid

15% of what we received, sent to your wallet within 24 hours of the payment clearing.

- 15% of every payment we receive from the project you introduced

- Paid in USDT — BEP-20 or ERC-20, straight to your wallet

- Nothing to sell — no quotas, no exclusivity, no upfront cost

- White-label friendly — if you're an agency, we never contact your client unless you ask us to

- Terms in writing before the first project, so nobody argues later

- One project or a steady flow — both are fine

Agencies: we'll sign a short referral agreement before the first project — scope, payment schedule, what you're owed and when. You're a partner, not a sales rep and not an employee.

## How it works

Short, because it should be. No forms to fill, no calls to schedule before we've even agreed it's a fit.

### You describe it

One message with what you want and when you need it. We reply with questions if anything's unclear.

### Fixed quote

A price and a deadline, in writing, before anything starts. You know the number up front.

### We build & show

You get a preview link early — not a surprise at the end. We adjust while it's still cheap to adjust.

### You get everything

Source code, setup docs and the deploy. Payment releases on escrow once you're happy.

      Payment is in crypto only: USDT on BEP-20 (BNB Chain) or ERC-20 (Ethereum / Base / Polygon) to the address below, or through escrow on LaborX if you'd rather not send funds first. No bank transfer, no PayPal, no card processor, no company invoices — which is exactly why we work this way. Not TRC-20: that wallet address does not exist on Tron.

## How an order actually happens

Four steps, and only the first one is yours.

        You

### 1. You email

A sentence or two is enough. What you want built, and when you need it. No form with twelve fields, no questionnaire, no call to schedule first.

        Us

### 2. You get a number

A fixed price and a delivery date, usually the same day. If the price from the table above applies, we say so. If your scope is bigger, we explain exactly what changed.

        Us

### 3. We build

Work starts after you agree the number in writing. You see progress as it happens rather than hearing about it at the end.

        You

### 4. You pay in USDT

BEP-20 or ERC-20 — never TRC-20, that address does not exist on Tron. The amount is fixed before we start, so nothing moves during the project.

        Us

### Source handed over

Repository and deployment are yours. You are never renting your own project back from us.

        Optional

### Care plan after launch

Backups, patches, uptime monitoring and a human who answers. $150 – $400 a month, cancel whenever.

## Straight answers

        Why are the prices fixed and published?

Because the usual agency dance — contact form, discovery call, forty-five minutes, then a number — wastes everyone's afternoon and usually ends in a quote nobody compares. Publishing the list filters out the people who were never going to buy and gets the ones who were straight to a decision.

        Do I have to book a call to see a price?

No. That is the entire point of this page. If the price fits, email us; if it doesn't, you found out in thirty seconds instead of an hour.

        How do I place an order?

You email hkay7645@gmail.com — type it into your own mail app, or use any "order →" link on this page. Send what you need and when you need it, and you get a fixed price and a delivery date back. There is no checkout, no account, and no payment taken before you have agreed the number.

        Why is payment in USDT?

Because cards and PayPal are unreliable or simply unavailable in the countries many of our clients work from. We take BEP-20 or ERC-20 only — never TRC-20, because that address does not exist on Tron and the transfer would be lost.

        What if my project is bigger than these packages?

Email the scope anyway. Larger work is quoted the same way: a fixed number agreed up front, broken into stages if that is easier. The price list is a starting point, not a ceiling.

        What if I want someone else to send you the client?

The partner program pays 15% of the fee on anything you send our way, with no cap and no exclusivity. It is described on the partners page.

      One sentence is enough

Market ranges are indicative only — they vary widely by region, agency size and how much discovery work is included. They exist here so you can check a quote, not as a promise from anyone. The dazo figure is our actual published price.

## What actually drives the price

Three things move a website quote more than everything else combined.

        Scope, not pages
        A 40-page brochure site can be cheaper than a 6-page one if the 6 pages need a booking engine. Count features, not URLs.

        Anything with a login
        Accounts, dashboards and data change the class of the work entirely. That is where most overruns happen.

        What runs after launch
        Lead capture, document processing and scheduled agents cost less than people assume and save far more than they cost.

## Questions this calculator cannot answer

### Why is a website ever $750 – $2,500?

Because it is one person with no account managers, no sales commission and no office overhead, using a proven build instead of rebuilding the wheel every time. What you do not pay for is the agency around the work. What you still get is the same deliverable and the same accountability.

### What makes a quote jump from the low end to the high end?

Logins, payments and integrations. Anything that has to remember who you are, take money, or talk to another system roughly doubles the work behind a page, and the estimate above reflects that.

### Is USDT payment actually workable for a business?

Yes, and it is the only way we can take payment reliably from several countries. We use BEP-20 or ERC-20 only — never TRC-20, because the fee behaviour and support vary too much. You receive a wallet address and a fixed amount before anything starts.

### Do I need to book a call to get the real price?

No. That is the point of this page. Send the scope, get the number, decide. If the number does not fit, you have lost two minutes rather than an afternoon.

### What if I want someone else to send you clients?

The partner program pays 15% of the fee on anything you send our way, with no cap and no exclusivity. It is described on the partners page.

      One sentence is enough

## What actually decides the price

        State, not messages
        A bot that must remember where each user stopped is a different project from one that replies to /start. That is the fork in the price.

        AI is cheaper than people expect
        The model costs less than the engineering around it. What costs money is handling the case where it answers confidently and wrongly.

        Bot plus website
        If the bot feeds a dashboard or a store, price both — combined builds share one backend and cost less than two separate ones.

## Common questions

### How long does a Telegram bot actually take?

Most of what people ask for is two to five days of work. The things that extend it are payments and anything that has to talk to a system you already run, because those are the parts that can fail in ways nobody notices until a customer does.

### Do I need a server to run it?

Yes, but it is smaller than people imagine. A well-written bot handling tens of thousands of messages a month fits comfortably on a small VPS. The hosting line above is a realistic range rather than a promotional number.

### Who owns the code?

You do. The repository and the deployment are handed over, so you are never renting your own bot from us.

### Can you take over a bot someone else wrote?

Yes. Send the repository and a description of what is broken. Partial rewrites are quoted as maintenance rather than a new build.

### Why is payment in USDT?

Because cards and PayPal are unreliable or unavailable for the countries many of our clients are in. We use BEP-20 or ERC-20 only — never TRC-20. The amount is fixed before work begins.

## Questions people actually ask

### Why does the same automation cost $900 or $3,000?

Number of systems it touches and whether a human has to approve anything. Two tools talking is fast. Five tools, with money moving and a person signing off, is a different build.

### What about the monthly cost of the AI itself?

API models usually run $10 – $80 a month at small volumes, and the dashboard we ship shows cost per run so it never surprises you. The self-hosted option removes that bill entirely.

### Is my data used for training?

No. We wire the build to a zero-retention API mode, or to a self-hosted model if the data cannot leave your servers at all.

### Can I start with one workflow and add more later?

That is how most projects start. The first build sets the patterns and the tests, so the second one is noticeably cheaper.

### Do I need a call to see the real number?

No. Send the scope, get the number, decide. If it does not fit, you lost two minutes instead of an afternoon.

## AI workflow automation

https://fyosamu.github.io/ai-automation/

AI Workflow Automation — n8n, Make & AI Agents | dazo

    AI workflow automation

# Stop being the API between your own tools

Integrations, AI agents, data sync and internal tools for SaaS teams and operators. Built on n8n, Make or straight Python/Node when the visual builder hits a wall — with the workflow definitions handed over so the automation is yours, not a subscription you rent forever.

      Describe your workflow
      See a shipped one

## What we automate

Integrations

### Connect the stack

Webhooks, OAuth, REST and GraphQL between your CRM, billing, helpdesk and sheets. Two-way sync with conflict rules — not a one-off zap that silently stops working in month two.

AI agents

### LLM pipelines that do a job

Classification, extraction, summarisation and routing over your own data. Retrieval over your docs, guardrails on the output, and a handoff to a human when confidence is low.

Automation

### n8n, Make or Zapier

Visual builders when they are enough, self-hosted n8n or plain Python when they are not. Either way you own the instance and the workflow files — exportable, versioned, not locked in.

Data

### Pipelines & sync

Scheduled jobs, dedupe, backfills and migrations between SaaS tools. Idempotent retries, so a dropped connection never duplicates a row or loses an order.

Internal

### Dashboards & approval flows

Admin panels, review queues and role-gated actions over the database you already have. The spreadsheet everyone edits becomes something with permissions and an audit trail.

Ops

### Reports & alerts

Daily digests, anomaly alerts, SLA watches and scheduled reports delivered to Slack or Telegram — without anyone assembling them by hand every morning.

## Proof, not a pitch

PostPilot, our own channel scheduler, is the standard we build your workflows to — and sd-gen, the AI video factory and our Instagram content pipeline are public repositories where an AI pipeline runs unattended on CI.

- Absolute, relative and recurring schedules that stay correct across timezones — the failure mode every automation gets wrong

- First poll records a baseline, so a newly connected source never floods your channel or your CRM with old records

- Rate-limit aware retries — a dropped connection stays pending and resumes instead of silently losing the work

- 40 automated tests, standard library only — no network in the suite, so a green run actually means something

- One runtime dependency, one SQLite file — it installs anywhere Python runs, no orchestration platform required

- Install docs and a 24/7 service setup included, because an automation that quietly stops is worse than no automation

## Questions people actually ask

      Do we have to use n8n?
No. Visual builders are right when the flow is linear and the connectors exist. When you hit rate limits, branching, custom auth or a retry the builder can't express, we drop to Python or Node. You own the instance and the workflow files either way.

      We have Zaps that keep breaking. Can you fix them?
Send us the failing one. Most breakages are expired auth, pagination the trigger never handled, or a rate limit with no backoff. We fix the root cause and add retries plus alerting, so it fails loudly instead of quietly at 3am.

      Can you work with our AI provider?
Yes — OpenAI, Anthropic, an open-weights model you host yourself, or whatever key you already have. Prompts, models and thresholds stay in config, so you can swap providers without a rewrite.

      Do you need access to our systems?
Least privilege: a service account with the narrowest scope that works, secrets kept in your vault, and the workflow definitions handed back to you at the end. You can revoke everything the day we finish.

      How do you price an automation?
Fixed quote after one message describing the workflow. If it turns out to be two projects, we say so and quote them separately rather than burying it in a number.

      Why do you only take crypto?
We don't have access to bank or card processors where we are. USDT on BEP-20 or ERC-20, or escrow on LaborX. No invoices with a company name, no chargebacks.

## Two ways to do it — pick with us, not for you

Most sites don't need a full rewrite. We tell you which route fits before you spend anything.

        Fastest

### Wrapped PWA

Your site becomes an installable progressive web app. Fastest to ship, easiest to update — changes go live instantly. Push notifications on Android; iOS support depends on the browser.

A thin native container around your site — real App Store and Play Store presence, push on both platforms, splash screens, deep links and offline caching.

        Full build

When the app needs to do things the site can't — camera, background sync, biometrics. We build it against the same backend, so nothing gets duplicated.

## Questions people actually ask

      Do I need to change my website first?
Usually not. We audit it first and tell you honestly if something will look broken inside an app shell. Small fixes are quoted separately so nothing is hidden.

      Will the app work if my site goes down?
The shell and cached content stay on the phone, so the app opens and shows what it has. Live data needs the site — the same dependency you already have.

      How much does it cost to publish on the App Store and Play Store?
The stores charge their own fees (Google Play is a one-time $25; Apple is $99/year). Those are paid by you, directly to Google and Apple — we never touch them.

Yes, and most clients do. We can hand you a signed build and the documentation, or submit it through your account if you give us access.

Overflow demand, clients asking for a site or an app, and no dev team to deliver it. You keep the relationship; we do the build.

### Freelancers who don't code

You close the deal and set your own margin on top. We build behind you and never contact your client.

### Community & channel owners

An audience is already half the sale. If your members ask for tools or sites, forward them to us.

### Consultants & media buyers

Add a delivery arm without hiring one. One introduction is enough to start.

## Web design studio? You design, we build.

Two studios in the same market are not competitors here — one of them sells the work, the other ships it. We would rather ship yours than pitch against you.

### Overflow, not rivalry

When your calendar fills up, hand us the build instead of declining the client. You keep the account, the retainer and every future redesign.

### Your brand only

White-label by default: your name on the proposal, the invoice and the launch announcement. Ours appears nowhere unless you ask us to show up.

### Either arrangement

Refer the project and keep 15% of our fee, or mark up our fixed price, invoice the client yourself and keep the difference.

What we take on: sites, stores, dashboards, the Android/iOS version of a site you already designed, Telegram and Discord bots, technical SEO and speed work. Every figure is published as a range at /pricing/, so you can price your own quote before you ever speak to us.

## The terms, in plain words

Everything below goes into a short written agreement before the first project, so nobody argues later.

### What you get

- 15% of every payment we receive from the project you introduced

- Paid in USDT — BEP-20 (BNB Chain) or ERC-20 (Ethereum / Base / Polygon), to your wallet

- Within 24 hours of each payment clearing, not at the end of some quarter

- Indefinite — one project or a steady flow, both fine

### What you don't get stuck with

- No joining fee, no subscription, no minimum quota

- No exclusivity — you can work with anyone else too

- No selling: we write the proposal, the quote and the contract

- No delivery risk — the build quality is ours, not yours

- No cold calling — we only ever contact a client you introduced

How we calculate it: 15% of the amount we actually receive on the project you introduced — not of a quote that was never paid. If the client only pays in stages, you get 15% of each stage as it clears.

Not TRC-20. Our wallets are EVM addresses. USDT must be sent on BEP-20 or ERC-20 — that address does not exist on Tron, and a TRC-20 transfer to it would be lost.

## Straight answers

        What if the client doesn't close?

Then there's nothing to pay and nothing owed. You only earn when we get paid, and we only get paid when the project ships and the client pays.

        Can I put my own price on top?

Yes. If you're selling the project as your own service, set whatever margin you like and invoice the client yourself. Our 15% is calculated on what we are paid by you.

        What kind of projects can I send?

Websites (theme or custom), turning an existing site into an Android/iOS app, Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp bots, technical SEO, performance work and site security. If it's outside that, ask anyway — we'll say no quickly if it is.

        Will you contact my client directly?

Not unless you ask us to. By default we talk to you, you talk to them. If you'd rather we run the account directly, we can — under a white-label arrangement.

        Why crypto only?

We're paid in USDT because we don't have access to bank or card processors in our jurisdiction. It also means no invoice delays and no chargebacks — the money you see clear is the money that's final.

        How do I know you'll actually pay?

You don't have to take our word for it: we'll put the 15% and the 24-hour window in writing before the first project, and every payment we receive from your introduction is on-chain and checkable. Start with one project.

# Fix the SEO issues search engines complain about

Not guesswork and not a 90-page PDF you will never open. We read what the crawl actually reports, tell you which problems are costing you visibility, and then fix them ourselves — schema, crawlability, indexing, internal linking and content structure.

      Get an audit quote
      See the full price list

## What we look at

Three groups, in the order they usually decide whether anything else you do can be seen at all.

        Found

### Crawl & indexation

robots.txt, sitemap, canonical tags, redirect chains, blocked resources, orphan pages, noindex mistakes and the pages Google has decided not to index at all.

        Understood

### Schema & on-page

Structured data that validates, headings that describe the page, titles and descriptions that match intent, image alt text, and the template-level issues that repeat on every page.

        Ranked

### Structure & internal links

Where link equity gets trapped, which pages should support which, category depth, duplicate content, thin templates and the content structure that keeps a topic coherent.

## What you get

- A written audit — every finding, why it matters and what we would do about it

- The fixes applied by us — not a checklist handed to your developer with no dates

- Before and after numbers — the crawl and the report re-run once the work is done

- Schema markup that validates — added or repaired, with the Rich Results test passing

- One template fix, every page — most of the gain sits in shared components, so we start there

- Source and access handed back — we work in your system, you keep everything

Honest disclaimer: nobody can guarantee a ranking. Anyone who does is either guessing or lying. What we guarantee is the audit, the fixes and the before/after numbers — the part that is actually under our control.

## Speed optimization

https://fyosamu.github.io/speed-optimization/

Website Speed Optimisation — Core Web Vitals | dazo

    Speed optimisation

# Make the page load before the visitor leaves

Every extra second of load time costs you the people who came to buy. We attack the file size, the render path and the server response — image pipelines, critical CSS, caching, CDN and bundle trimming — and we measure it twice so you can see what changed.

      Get a speed quote
      See the full price list

## Where the time usually goes

Slow sites are rarely slow for a mysterious reason. These four account for most of what we find.

        Bytes

### Unoptimized media

PNGs where WebP or AVIF belongs, hero images the size of a phone screen served at four times that, no lazy loading, and video that autoplays above the fold.

        Render

### Blocking CSS and JS

Stylesheets and scripts the page cannot paint without, third-party tags loading in the critical path, and a bundle shipping libraries that are used once.

        Server

### Slow response

Uncached pages generated from scratch on every request, no CDN in front of static assets, and database work repeated because a query was never indexed.

        Measure

### Core Web Vitals, not vibes

LCP, INP and CLS are the numbers Google actually uses. We read them from field data where it exists — real visitors, real devices — rather than a lab test on a fast desktop connection.

## What you get

- A Lighthouse run before and after — two dated reports, so the improvement is a fact, not a claim

- Images rebuilt properly — modern formats, responsive sizes, lazy loading below the fold

- Critical CSS inlined, the rest deferred — the page paints without waiting for a stylesheet

- Bundle trimmed — unused code removed, heavy libraries replaced or loaded only where needed

- Caching and CDN configured — repeat visits and static assets stop hitting the origin

- Nothing added that you now have to maintain — no new framework, no proprietary plugin

Honest disclaimer: we do not promise a specific Lighthouse score, because the final number depends on your hosting and on third-party tags we do not control. We promise the measured before/after and the work that produced it.

## How it works

### Send the URL

We run the audit and tell you which of the four causes is actually costing you time on your site.

### Fixed quote

Flat price before any work starts. $400 – $1,200, delivered in 1 to 3 days.

### We optimise

Media, render path, bundle and server response — in your codebase, with the changes visible in version history.

### Measure again

A second Lighthouse run at handover, with the numbers written into the delivery note alongside the first.

$400 – $1,200

typical range — 1 to 3 days

0

new frameworks added to your project

Changes are made in a way you can review and revert, and the site is checked after each round. Anything that would alter how the site looks or behaves gets flagged first rather than quietly shipped.

The URL for the audit. Applying the fixes needs the source — a repository, or the CMS if the site is built on one. If your developer would rather do it, we can hand over a prioritised list instead, though the price stays the same.

    Care plan

# Someone who answers after launch

Most sites do not get hacked or broken by a big change. They rot — an outdated plugin here, a backup nobody checked there, a certificate that expired on a Sunday. This plan is the person watching for that, $150 – $400 a month, cancel whenever.

      Start the care plan
      See the full price list

## What happens every month

Not a dashboard you are supposed to check yourself — actual work, done whether or not you log in.

        Restore point

### Backups

Taken on a schedule and stored away from the site itself, so a broken deploy or a compromised host does not take the backup with it. Periodically restored, because an untested backup is a guess.

        Patched

### Updates

Core, plugin and dependency updates applied deliberately rather than left to auto-update at 3am. Anything risky gets tested first, and we do not install a new major version the day it appears.

        Woken up

### Uptime monitoring

The site is checked continuously. If it goes down you hear from us rather than finding out from a customer — and if the cause is on our side, we start on it.

        Human

### Support that replies

Small change you need made? A question about something breaking? You email a person, not a ticket queue with a four-day autoresponder. That is most of what people are actually buying.

## What you get

- Scheduled off-site backups — and a restore that has actually been tested

- Core, plugin and dependency patches — applied and checked, not queued

PostPilot — Telegram Scheduler Bot with RSS Auto-Posting, $79 | dazo

      product · ready to ship

# PostPilot — your Telegram channel, on autopilot

A framework-free Python bot that schedules posts to any Telegram channel and auto-publishes new RSS and Atom items. One runtime dependency, one SQLite file, and a 40-test suite that runs on the standard library alone.

$79 — source + docs, delivered same day

        Request the source →

## What it does

### Post scheduling

Absolute times, relative delays and recurring schedules — all timezone-correct. Queue a week of posts in one sitting and let it publish.

### RSS / Atom auto-posting

Point it at any feed. New items get published to your channel automatically, with a baseline on first poll so old articles never flood it.

### Rate-limit aware

Telegram rate limits are retried, not dropped. A network hiccup leaves the post pending instead of losing it.

### Runs anywhere

Any Linux box, a $5 VPS, or a Raspberry Pi. State is one SQLite file — back it up by copying it.

## What is inside

- Full source code — no obfuscation, no license server, no phone-home

- Install docs — from empty server to publishing in one sitting

- 24/7 service setup — systemd unit so it survives reboots

- 40-test suite — runs on the Python standard library alone

- Test run recording — watch it work before you deploy it

      # scheduling is plain and readable
from postpilot import Scheduler

sched = Scheduler(db="channel.db")
sched.at("2026-11-01 09:00", tz="Europe/Berlin", text="weekly drop is live")
sched.every("monday 08:30", tz="Asia/Tehran", file="posts/monday.md")
sched.watch_rss("https://blog.example.com/feed", channel="@mystore")

The complete source, install documentation, a 24/7 service setup guide, and a recorded test run. Delivered by email the same day.

        What are the runtime requirements?

Python 3.10+, one runtime dependency (feedparser), and a Telegram bot token. No database server, no Docker.

        Will old RSS items flood my channel?

No. The first poll only records a baseline. Only items that appear after it are ever published.

        Can I use it for client projects?

Yes. It is your source after purchase — modify it, rebrand it, deploy it for as many channels as you want.
